quarterly_data.quarter: Marvell press release: ADDING and REPLACING Marvell Unveils Second-generation (10-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Marvell announced the second-generation Structera X 3406 and Structera X 3506 CXL 3.2 memory expansion controllers (its claim: industry-first six-channel CXL memory expanders): six DDR4/DDR5 channels (50% more than the prior generation) and PCIe Gen 6 connectivity, supporting up to 9TB of DDR4 (Structera X 3406, 18 DDR4 RDIMM slots) or 6TB of DDR5 (Structera X 3506, 12 DDR5 RDIMM slots) per controller; memory sharing with up to four hosts at up to 256GB/s of host bandwidth; and inline LZ4 compression at up to 250GB/s for up to 2-3x more effective capacity. Marvell cites up to 40-50% faster time to first token at equivalent context length versus the previous generation. The Structera X 3406 and 3506 are expected to sample in Q1 2027 (demoed at the OCP Summit), extending the first-generation Structera X 2404 and 2504 architecture already shipping to hyperscalers.
quarterly_data.figure: six DDR4/DDR5 channels; up to 9TB DDR4 / 6TB DDR5 per controller; up to 250GB/s compression; sampling expected Q1 2027

quarterly_data.quarter: Marvell press release: ADDING and REPLACING Marvell Unveils Second-generation (10-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Will Chu (EVP and GM, Custom Cloud Solutions): Marvell is 'the only provider with a complete end-to-end CXL portfolio' spanning memory expansion (Structera X), near-memory acceleration (Structera A) and the Photonic Fabric Memory Appliance (PFMA) pod-scale CXL memory-sharing appliance, and 'We are delivering industry-leading CXL controllers, co-developed with leading hyperscalers.' The release carries supporting statements from AMD (collaboration building on AMD EPYC processors), Arm (Structera X brings CXL 3.2 to the Arm ecosystem), Alibaba and Meta (each working with Marvell on CXL memory solutions), and Samsung Electronics and SK hynix (Structera validated or deployable with their DDR memory).
